articles.title: How new cooling technologies could cut AC electricity demand
articles.description: America's answer to hotter summers has overwhelmingly been more air conditioning, and engineers are now looking for ways to keep people cool without driving up electricity demand. Why it matters: The need for cooling is surging. The issue isn't just how to generate more electricity — it's how to use less of it and ease demand when grids are most strained. Between the lines: A July study finds that keeping buildings cool without relying solely on AC will be critical for adapting to climate change. AC is already nearly ubiquitous in the U.S., but that doesn't mean its electricity consumption has peaked. "The market is saturated, but the use of air conditioning or the energy consumption for air conditioning will increase because of the overheating," Mat Santamouris, a University of New South Wales professor and the study's lead author, tells Axios. Higher temperatures mean Americans will run AC more, while cooling is becoming increasingly necessary in northern parts of the country that historically needed less of it. Threat level: More AC means more electricity demand at the very moments the grid is under the most pressure. AC can account for roughly half of total peak electricity demand on the hottest days in Texas, according to an International Energy Agency analysis . Ankit Kalanki, lead cooling expert at clean-energy nonprofit RMI, tells Axios that "saving 1 kilowatt-hour of energy at midnight is not the same as reducing 1 kilowatt of peak demand at 6 p.m. when everyone is coming back from the office and turning on the air conditioner." The big picture: Meeting America's growing need for cooling doesn't have to mean supplying all of it with more electricity. "We really have to avoid the solar radiation [entering] the building," Santamouris says. Letting that heat in and then spending electricity to remove it, he adds, "is not so intelligent." State of play: The options largely fall into three categories: Keep heat out, cool more efficiently and ease demand on the grid. That includes smart windows and shading to block heat, reflective roof coatings, built-in energy storage to ease peak demand, and automation and ventilation to cut down on AC use. In Colorado , RMI and Boulder County are testing passive daytime radiative cooling paint on roofs. Kalanki calls it "a more advanced version" of white paint: It reflects sunlight while also radiating heat into the sky. Blue Frontier's air conditioners use a liquid desiccant to remove moisture from the air and built-in energy storage to reduce power use during peak-demand hours. Yes, but: There's no single cooling equivalent of double-pane windows. The right mix of cooling technologies depends on climate, building type and location, Santamouris says. Case in point: A 2024 study co-authored by Santamouris modeled heat-mitigation strategies in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, and found that combining cool materials and greenery could reduce peak ambient temperatures by up to 4.5°C. Reality check: None of these technologies eliminates the need for AC, which can save lives during extreme heat. The goal is to reduce how frequently and intensely it operates. The bottom line: "Efficiency is the cheapest resource that we have available," Kalanki says, because reducing demand can avoid the need for new generation, transmission and distribution infrastructure. Go deeper: The U.S. just had its hottest month on record

articles.title: PML-N secures 5 out of 7 reserved seats up for grabs in AJK Legislative Assembly
articles.description: MUZAFFARABAD: The PML-N bagged five while the PPP won two of the seven reserved seats that were up for grabs in the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Legislative Assembly on Monday. Under Article 22(1) of the AJK Constitution, the Legislative Assembly consists of 53 members, including 45 members elected directly through adult franchise and eight members chosen by directly elected representatives. The reserved seats include five seats for women and one each for Ulema-i-Din or Mashaikh well-versed in the teachings of Islam, Jammu and Kashmir State subjects residing abroad, and technocrats and other professionals. PML-N’s Chaudhry Abdul Rehman Arain was the only candidate to have submitted his nomination papers for the seat reserved for state subjects residing abroad. He was consequently declared elected unopposed. After polling for the remaining seats on Monday, PML-N’s Sehrish Qamar, Maryam Idrees and Maryam Zaman, also known as Maryam Kashmiri, secured one seat each reserved for women. Seven votes were polled for each of them, as were for PPP’s Farzana Yaqoob, who claimed the fourth reserved seat for women. There were just two more contenders — PML-N’s Riffat Abid and PPP’s Zobia Khurshid Raja — vying for the seats for women whose votes were tied at five. Eventually, Raja was declared the winner for the last seat left, with the result being decided by drawing lots. For the seat reserved for Ulema and Mashaikh, PML-N’s Mohammad Mazhar Saeed won against his sole contender, PPP’s Hafiz Tariq Mahmood, after garnering 26 votes — almost double than Mahmood’s 12. Similarly, PML-N’s Barrister Syed Iftikhar Gillani also bagged 26 votes to claim the seat reserved for technocrats and professionals, beating PPP’s Sahibzada Zulfiqar Ali by 14 votes. In days preceding Monday’s polls, elections to seven of the 45 directly elected seats — five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district — could not be held due to the law and order situation in the region. As a result, the 38 members elected so far, representing 84.4 per cent of the directly elected membership, participated in the reserved seat elections. As the inaugural session of the incoming Legislative Assembly has already been summoned for 2pm on Monday, shortly after the announcement of the results, all newly elected members are expected to take an oath at the hands of outgoing Speaker Chaudhry Latif Akbar, who failed to retain his seat in the elections. AJK polls The elections in the region, originally scheduled for July 27, were divided into phases over security concerns amid unrest in the region. The first phase was held on July 27, the second on Aug 2 and the third on Aug 10. The third phase was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division, which comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district. However, the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli because of concerns over the law and order situation. So far, in the direct elections to 38 constituencies, the PML-N has secured 25 seats while the PPP won 12. The lone MLA-elect of the Awami Dast-o-Bazu party has also joined hands with the PML-N . The PPP has alleged widespread rigging in the polls, with the party also ramping up its criticism of the ruling PML-N in recent days. Last week, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said that a genuine alliance with the PML-N was not possible until their grievances regarding the AJK polls were addressed as he established formal contact with the PTI and offered to cooperate with the party in Parliament. Speaking to the media, the PPP chairman alleged that the AJK election process had been made controversial for political interests. He alleged that the federal government’s political and administrative machinery had remained active in AJK throughout the six-phase election process, raising serious questions over its transparency. The PPP, he said, had raised its objections before the Election Commission, parliament and other constitutional forums, but the PML-N had failed to address its concerns or engage in meaningful dialogue after the polls. Moreover, he said the commitments and political understandings reached with the PML-N before the prime minister’s election had not been honoured. The PPP had cooperated in the wider national interest, he said, but there could be no genuine alliance with the PML-N unless the party’s concerns over the AJK elections were addressed and political commitments fulfilled. He pointed out that the government needed PPP’s votes for several important laws, constitutional amendments and difficult bills. He said legislation could not be forced through on the basis of a majority or through coercion. The discord between the PPP and PML-N was also apparent in the National Assembly on Aug 18, when the former managed to compel the government to virtually suspend the heavy legislative agenda for the day, which included 21 bills. On Aug 20, when the lower house of Parliament passed two bills pertaining to the military and nuclear command structure, the PPP also objected to the manner in which the legislation was presented. While the party ultimately voted in favour of the bills, Bilawal lashed out at the government for not taking ruling allies on board.

articles.title: Marine Le Pen's career has been resurrected – and she is a bigger threat than ever | Mujtaba Rahman
articles.description: No longer banned from next year’s presidential election, Le Pen is a far more formidable force than her understudy, Jordan Bardella France loves a battle-scarred survivor. Charles de Gaulle, François Mitterrand and Jacques Chirac clawed their way back from political failure to become presidents of the republic. There is a significant chance that Marine Le Pen will be next. Now that the Paris appeal court has unshackled her from an electoral ban for fraud, the far-right veteran has double appeal in the race for the French presidency next year. She will run, as always, as an outsider and a scourge of the political elites – despite continuously holding electoral office since 1998. She can also now pose as a “miraculous survivor”, a “mother courage” and “a battling granny”, as senior French political figures, including former ministers, described her to me during recent conversations in Paris. Mujtaba Rahman is the managing director for Europe at Eurasia Group, a political risk research and consulting firm Continue reading...

articles.title: Trump snubbed at GOP convention as his own party won't say his name: report
articles.description: President Donald Trump's name was barely mentioned at a Michigan GOP convention over the weekend, even as the party sought to present a " unified strategy " to voters, according to a new report. The Detroit Free Press reported that the Aug. 22 nominating convention inside the Soaring Eagle Casino & Resort in Mt. Pleasant was full of Trumpian attacks on Democrats — blaming them for issues ranging from schools to roads and the electric grid — but the leader of the national party was conspicuously absent. Even Republicans like Senate candidate Mike Rogers, attorney general nominee Doug Lloyd, and Secretary of State candidate Anthony Forlini avoided using Trump's name in their speeches, according to the report. "Asked why neither he nor any of the other candidates mentioned Trump, Sen. Jim Runestad, R-White Lake, the state party chairman, pointed to Michigan's poor performance on student testing and the condition of Michigan roads," the report reads. "'We can't do anything about what's happening at the national level,' Runestad said. 'We need to be focused on what we can do here on the state of Michigan.'" Runestad's comments also starkly contrast with the plea Trump made to voters during a rally last Friday for Darline Graham , who is running to replace her late brother, Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-SC), in the Senate. Trump recalled how analysts have said Republicans perform poorly when Trump isn't on the ballot. "Please, pretend I am on the ballot," Trump told the audience.
